answers.hi: Hi! 👋 How can I help you with your agriculture analysis today? Whether it's crop classification, NDVI trends, or field segmentation, I'm here to assist. 🌾
answers.What is NDVI?: NDVI stands for Normalized Difference Vegetation Index. It’s a measure of vegetation health calculated from satellite data using the red and near-infrared light reflected by plants. Values range from -1 to 1, with healthy crops typically showing values above 0.3. Higher NDVI means more green vegetation, which helps us monitor crop growth and health over time.
answers.How does change detection work?: Change detection works by comparing the NDVI (vegetation health) values from two different years—typically the peak growing seasons—across the same area. It calculates the difference in NDVI between those years, highlighting areas where vegetation has increased (e.g., new crops or regrowth) or decreased (e.g., crop loss or land degradation). This helps identify shifts in land use or crop patterns over time.
